column1: # 121 instructions; .pdata declares 121 and listing_against_pdata reports short=0.
# Called once per player by 0x82211DF8 with:
# IT READS THE RECORD WITH THE RULE THE PRODUCT ALREADY IMPLEMENTS:
# 1318 from the PRODUCER's bit-scan and ported at 1323. Here it is again, in the
# CONSUMER, read from a function that shares nothing with that derivation.
# THE SHAPE: two nested loops of 32.
#   outer r26 over 32 output slots, gated by [player+0x88] & (1 << r26)
#   the mask for slot r26 is [player + 0x08 + 4*r26]
#   inner r30 over the 32 bits of that mask -- each set bit names a RECORD bit
#   the binding descriptor is 24 bytes at player + 24 * (bit + 6)
# THE AXIS RULE, read instruction by instruction:
#   f13 = fsel(value, f0, -f0)                 the sign of the input restored
# A SECOND OUTPUT, from the same record slot:
#   so it is a three-state sign, not a magnitude.
# Then, when [player+0x8C] & (1 << r26), BOTH outputs are negated; they are
# written into the caller's arrays at r31 and r31+r23; and [r5] |= (1 << r26).
# The last two are the same words cycles 1330 and 1342 already identified.
# NOT ESTABLISHED: what the four output arrays are consumed by; what `this` is;
# why the descriptor index starts at +6; whether all 32 output slots are used.
